title: agent-core: deterministic timing in two Windows-flaky tests
head: flaky-windows-timing
body:
## What

Two tests failed on GitHub's `windows-latest` runner on a PR that did not touch them, then passed on rerun. Both were timing assumptions too tight for a loaded/slow CI runner, not product bugs.

- `tests/test_models_private_ledger.py::test_concurrent_processes_lose_no_charges_or_alert_thresholds` spawns 3 real OS processes (`multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`) hammering one `FileLedger` concurrently. Every `begin`/`settle`/`claim_alerts` call goes through `FileLedger._transaction`, which acquires a single global `filelock.FileLock` configured with the product's `LOCK_TIMEOUT = 5.0` (`src/anorak/models/private_ledger.py`). On a loaded `windows-latest` runner, process-spawn cost plus fsynced-append contention across 3 processes doing 18 lock-protected transactions total can push a legitimate (not stuck) lock wait past 5s; when that happens `filelock.Timeout` is caught by `_transaction`'s broad `except Exception` and re-raised as `AccountingUncertain`, which `_concurrent_spend`'s `except Exception` turns into `("failed", [])` -- exactly the `status != "ok"` the test caught. Fix: each spawned child now sets its own copy of `private_ledger.LOCK_TIMEOUT` to a generous 60s before opening the ledger. This has to happen inside the child, not via a parent-process `monkeypatch.setattr` (the existing in-process pattern already used lower in this same file for `MAX_JOURNAL_BYTES`), because `"spawn"` re-imports the module fresh in the child process and would not see a parent-side patch. Also widened the test's own `start.wait`/`results.get`/`process.join` timeouts to match, so a real deadlock (which the test still exists to catch) would still time the test out, just at a larger, CI-realistic bound. The test still proves the same property: no charge or alert threshold is lost under genuinely concurrent processes.
- `tests/test_models_t07_acceptance.py::test_t07_skill_runs_unchanged_and_cost_appears_in_the_log[openrouter]` got `result.status == "max_seconds"` instead of `"done"`. The acceptance skill's `Budget(max_steps=5, max_seconds=5.0, max_usd=...)` gives `LoopRunner.run` a real wall-clock deadline (`src/anorak/loop.py`: `deadline = self._clock() + skill.budget.max_seconds`, enforced by both `check_deadline()` and an outer `asyncio.timeout(...)`) -- but this test's HTTP call is a `httpx.MockTransport` that answers instantly; the 5s budget was never meant to be exercised, only left no slack for import/process/fsynced-ledger-write overhead under a loaded runner. Fix: raised to `max_seconds=30.0`, matching this repo's other skill fixtures (`tests/fixtures/skills/*/skill.yaml` use 30-60s). The test still proves the skill runs unchanged and cost lands in the log; it is not a test of the max_seconds cutoff itself (that's covered separately in `tests/test_loop.py`).

No real product bug: both timeouts (`LOCK_TIMEOUT=5.0`, and a skill author's own `max_seconds`) are reasonable defaults for a single user's machine; the tightness only showed up under GitHub's shared/loaded Windows runner plus the test's own multi-process/full-loop overhead. Both fixes are test-only -- confirmed by `git diff` touching only `tests/` and `CHANGELOG.md`, so the version stays `0.7.28`.

## Mutation check

| test | mutant | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_concurrent_processes_lose_no_charges_or_alert_thresholds` | `private_ledger.py`'s settle-path totals update (`state.totals[agent] = _sum(state.totals.get(agent, Decimal(0)), cost)`) changed to drop the charge (`state.totals[agent] = state.totals.get(agent, Decimal(0))`) | Still fails: `AssertionError: assert Decimal('0') == Decimal('4500')` on `store.total(agent())`. Reverted; `git diff` confirmed clean restore. |
| `test_t07_skill_runs_unchanged_and_cost_appears_in_the_log[openrouter]` | `loop.py`'s `emit("action", "completed")` call (which logs the completed action's cost) removed from the action loop | Still fails: `assert len(completed) == 1` -> `assert 0 == 1`. Reverted; `git diff` confirmed clean restore. |

Both mutants applied to the real product file, target test re-run to confirm the expected failure, then restored via `cp`/diff-verified copy (not `git stash`).

## Tests

```
uv run pytest -q tests/test_models_private_ledger.py::test_concurrent_processes_lose_no_charges_or_alert_thresholds "tests/test_models_t07_acceptance.py::test_t07_skill_runs_unchanged_and_cost_appears_in_the_log[openrouter]"
2 passed

uv run pytest -q
2671 passed, 5 skipped, 1 deselected in 155.24s (ran twice, both clean)

uv run ruff check .
All checks passed!

uv run mypy --strict src
Success: no issues found in 56 source files
```

Flake-gone verification (loop in shell, `--count` isn't available):
- `test_concurrent_processes_lose_no_charges_or_alert_thresholds`: 30/30 solo; 4 copies run in parallel x 30 iterations each = 120/120 under CPU load.
- `test_t07_skill_runs_unchanged_and_cost_appears_in_the_log[openrouter]`: 30/30 solo; 4 copies run in parallel x 30 iterations each = 120/120 under CPU load.

Version stayed `0.7.28` -- no product code changed (`git diff --stat`: `tests/test_models_private_ledger.py`, `tests/test_models_t07_acceptance.py`, `CHANGELOG.md` only). `CHANGELOG.md` updated under `## Unreleased`.
